title: Cell: Chapter Introduction
subject: Biology
objective: You began as a single cell. Every living thing is built of cells: how they were discovered, what is inside, how they divide, and the cell theory.

fill.q: The basic structural and functional unit of life is the ____.
The word "cell" was first used by ____ in 1665.
The outer boundary of an animal cell is the cell ____.
The part of the cell that controls its activities is the ____.
An amoeba is made of ____ cell.

tf.q: Every living thing is made of cells.
tf.explain: Cell theory: all organisms consist of one or more cells.

tf.q: Hooke saw living cells in cork.
tf.explain: Cork cells are dead; Hooke saw their empty walls.

tf.q: New cells can form from non-living matter.
tf.explain: New cells arise only from pre-existing cells.

tf.q: One cell divides to give two cells.

ar.a: You began life as a single cell.
ar.r: A human starts as one cell that divides again and again.

ar.a: Cells are called the building blocks of life.
ar.r: All living things are built from cells.

mcq.q: Hooke observed cells in a thin slice of:
mcq.explain: He looked at cork under his microscope.
Its whole body is one cell.
They are organelles inside the cell.

mcq.q: After three rounds of division, one cell becomes:

short.q: State the three points of cell theory.
short.solution: All living things are made of cells; the cell is the basic unit of life; new cells arise from pre-existing cells.

short.q: Name three parts of an animal cell and the job of each.
short.solution: Cell membrane: boundary that controls what enters and leaves. Nucleus: controls the cell and holds genetic material. Mitochondria: release energy.
